commits.message:
feat(color): text keeps its contrast at 256 colours; downgrades never pick terminal-defined ANSI 0-15

A downgrade to 256 colours matched against all 256 entries, so it could land
on ANSI 0-15, whose RGB every terminal theme redefines, and Style.toSgrCodes
rounded text and background independently, so two roundings could meet in
the middle: a 4.57:1 pair drew at 3.25:1.

- EIGHT_BIT_DOWNGRADE_TABLE holds the cube and grey ramp (16-255); ColorTable
  takes a firstIndex so its matches are terminal indices.
- ColorTable.matchReadable: the nearest entry that clears a ratio against a
  background, else the most contrast.
- ColorSpec.downgradeOn(target, bg): at 256 colours text keeps the contrast
  the truecolor pair had (or the most the palette offers on the drawn bg);
  elsewhere the drawn RGB is the terminal's and text downgrades alone.
- relativeLuminance/contrastRatio move to core/color.ts, below both the
  theme math and the SGR writer; themes/colorMath re-exports them.

chore(release)!: 0.12.0 (#154)

BREAKING CHANGE: PowerlineJoinerOptions requires glyph and divider together (#153). A caller that replaced only the arrow must also pass a divider; new PowerlineJoiner() draws POWERLINE_JOINER_GLYPHS.
